newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: India's NDDB in Sri Lanka milk joint venture.
newsitem.headline: India's NDDB in Sri Lanka milk joint venture.

text.p: India's National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) will take a majority shareholding in a dairy plant being set up in a joint venture with the Sri Lankan government to produce 300,000 litres of milk per day.

Sri Lanka's Minister for Trade, Commerce and Food Kingsley Wickramaratna told a news conference on Thursday that the joint venture will mainly process liquid milk and help upgrade capacities of the existing dairy plants in the island.
The new joint venture will be called Kiriya Milk Industries of Lanka Ltd and the total project cost is estimated at 1.09 billion rupees.

Indian officials said New Delhi will provide a credit line of 256 million rupees and another 567 million rupees will be raised through long-term loans. NDDB and the Sri Lankan government will finance the remaining capital through equity.
NDDB is one of India's biggest milk and milk products producers and the Sri Lankan venture is its first overseas investment.

Wickramaratna said NDDB will also invest some 150 million rupees in a new cattle feed plant and a urea molasses plant. He said the joint venture will launch a programme to increase local milk production by encouraging the participation of small farmers through cooperative networks.
"NDDB will hold back its profits in Sri Lanka and plough them back in the joint venture for the next 10 years," Wickramaratne said.

Sri Lanka currently produces some 200 million litres of milk annually, which meets only 25 percent of local demand. The rest, moslty milk powder, is imported at a cost of 3.5 billion rupees annually, Wickramaratna said.
